audience: operators running several coding agents on one repository who need a shared answer to who decides, who is working, and how work gets approved
maintainers hot-loading multi-agent coordination into a working repo with one command that fails closed on a partial install
teams that want coordination rules pinned as documents and a validator, not an agent that decides on their behalf
problem: Put more than one agent on a single repository and the hard problem stops being the code. Two agents claim the same task, a seat goes quiet and nobody notices for an hour, an agent drafts a change nobody approved, or a returning agent acts on a lease it no longer holds. The work itself is fine; the coordination is not. There is no shared, written answer to who is boss, how a seat fails over, or how a proposed change earns a PR.
solution: ACS ships the multi-agent hotloader: a versioned coordination pack that, dropped into any working repo, wires join-order roles, a decision boss on a minute-scale lease with FIFO failover, a claim queue, an agent-less watchdog, and a propose -> boss ACCEPT/REJECT -> claim -> PR path, on top of the full Project Continuity Modules (PCM) and full Content Generation Modules (CGM 0.5.12) contracts, without vendoring either helper's source.
mechanism: join/continue order fills roles (first continuer = decision boss, next = coder1, ...); the assignment seed is a hint only and tool identity is irrelevant

the decision boss holds a lease measured in minutes (default 30, range 15-120); after the TTL the seat is vacant, claimants form a FIFO claim queue, and the front takes boss; a returning old boss rejoins at the end with no automatic reclaim
an agent-less watchdog runs every ~10 minutes and only flags a stale seat - it never appoints a boss or makes a product decision (watchdog != failover)
work moves proposal -> boss ACCEPT/REJECT -> claim branch -> PR; nothing commits straight to the protected default branch and required CI gates must pass on the exact candidate
hotload_check resolves the pinned PCM and CGM checkouts, runs the adapter validator, and only on success writes PROMPT_INJECT.md; missing or stale pins fail closed
pins.json is the single source of truth and check_pins.py fails closed when any declared projection disagrees on a PCM/CGM commit, version family, or the eight-module count

evidence.claim: The multi-agent hotloader is the install surface and fails closed on a partial install: FULL PCM + FULL CGM 0.5.12 + this runtime, with a thin subset rejected on purpose.
evidence.supports: The pack's entry document states the three full-stack install requirements, the load order, and that hotload_check.py fails the install unless the assignment pins, the helper checkout revision, and the adapter validation all pass.
evidence.limits: A specification and a validator do not guarantee adopter agents honor every rule; enforcement depends on the adopter enabling branch protection and required checks.

evidence.claim: Pin drift is caught, not assumed: pins.json is the single source of truth and check_pins.py fails closed on any declared projection that disagrees.
evidence.supports: The checker reads pins.json, scans every declared projection, and exits non-zero on a foreign commit token, a wrong version family, a missing module-count word, or a superseded value - even when the canonical value is also present. CI runs it on every candidate.
evidence.limits: It verifies that declared projections agree with the manifest; it cannot see a surface that was never declared as a projection.

evidence.claim: Roles fill by live join order, the boss holds a minute-scale lease with FIFO failover, and the watchdog is liveness-only - all written down as binding.
evidence.supports: ROLES.md specifies join-order role fill, the lease TTL (default 30 minutes, range 15-120), the GitHub-canonical FIFO claim queue, the returning-boss-rejoins-at-end rule, the zombie-boss rule, and that the ~10-minute watchdog flags a stale seat without appointing a boss.
evidence.limits: A written process is a commitment, not an enforcement mechanism; it relies on agents and operators reading the same document.

evidence.claim: Proposals gate the path to a PR: propose -> boss ACCEPT/REJECT -> claim branch -> PR, with no direct commits to the protected default branch.
evidence.supports: PROPOSALS.md defines the proposal lifecycle and the boss ACCEPT/REJECT gate that turns an accepted proposal into a claim on a branch and then a PR, keeping the proposal/ACCEPT layer out of PCM's scope.
evidence.limits: Relies on the adopter enabling branch protection and required checks; the ACCEPT/REJECT gate is a governance rule, not an automated judge.

evidence.claim: The adapter pins the full content-generation contract at 0.5.12 (eight modules including human-output-naming) and the pack pins PCM CLI 0.6.0, both fail-closed.
evidence.supports: system-version.json pins helper 0.5.12 @ 6831f91e165b62d719c05eb492f7375fa932b560 with the eight-module list; the pack's pins.json independently pins PCM CLI 0.6.0 @ 4e2385474b4af9249ca009cbdcb38c4498932475, and check_pins.py holds both.
evidence.limits: The pins are exact and fail-closed; they do not claim the adopter's prose meets the writing contract, only that the correct modules are loaded.

boundaries: ACS owns execution coordination only; it ships no decision-making, adjudication, or benchmarking layer, and makes no decisions on an agent's behalf
ACS does not replace PCM or CGM and does not vendor helper source trees
The boss ACCEPT/REJECT gate is a governance rule, not an automated judge; final authority belongs to the human operator
No API keys, tokens, cookies, or .env contents enter the repository; external keys are referenced by environment-variable name only
Live status as of 2026-10-04: the registry ships exactly one module (multi-agent-hotload @ 0.1.0); decision-making and benchmarking work is parked outside this repository
